solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Writing from time to time

parts.note: T again abbreviates time
ex means from, as in goods sold ex works
T again abbreviates time

explanation.surface: Someone writes only now and then, in fits and starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from time to time' reads as an idiom for occasionally, but it is a recipe: T, then EX (from), then another T.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: any written words on a page make up a body of printed matter.

clue.text: Mellow temperature? It's high for exercising

indicators.note: exercising puts the letters through their paces, working them into a new order

explanation.surface: A mild temperature? It's high for a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercising' rearranges ITSHIGH. 'Mellow' means pleasantly drunk, not mild.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: mellow means slightly drunk, a little merry or tipsy.

clue.text: Short distance in unfinished Italian port is most tidy

indicators.note: in places one thing within another
unfinished means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: Trieste is a port in north-east Italy
MM, millimetres, are a short distance

explanation.surface: A tiny distance within an incomplete Italian port is the neatest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' drops the final E of TRIESTE, and MM goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: neat and orderly to the greatest degree, the superlative of a word for neat.

clue.text: Remark about German with loyalty

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the remark goes round the German word

parts.note: a remark is a comment
mit is the German word for with

explanation.surface: An observation regarding a German who is faithful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German with' is not a German person plus a link word: it asks for the German translation of 'with'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: steadfast loyalty is dedication or a pledged attachment to a cause or person.

clue.text: Bill upset in necklace perhaps causing inflammation

indicators.note: in puts the jumbled name inside the necklace

parts.note: a necklace is one example of a chain

indicators.note: upset says the letters of the name are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Bill gets annoyed when a necklace causes a rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns BILL into ILBL, which goes 'in' CHAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a painful itchy swelling of the skin brought on by cold, usually on fingers or toes.

clue.text: Only food emperor chewed: a piece of cake?

indicators.note: chewed says the words are munched up and their letters mashed together

explanation.surface: An emperor who ate nothing but food, asking whether it was easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: payment for a task that is effortless, a piece of cake to do.

clue.text: Warm heart confused with beginnings of mutual love

indicators.note: confused says the letters are mixed up
beginnings of means the first letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A warm heart muddled by the first stirrings of shared love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' shuffles HEART together with M and L, the 'beginnings of' mutual love.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: thermal clothing keeps you warm; the word describes heat retention.

clue.text: Going west in Spain, St Anthony's cross with warning from Rome to move away from danger

indicators.note: in an across-style reading, going west means running right to left, backwards

parts.note: E is the vehicle code for Spain
St Anthony's cross is the T-shaped tau cross
cave is Latin for beware, a warning in Roman speech

explanation.surface: Heading west through Spain, a cross-bearing pilgrim gets a Latin alarm and flees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going west' reverses the whole string E + TAU + CAVE. CAVE (Latin 'beware') was schoolboy slang for a lookout's warning.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to leave a dangerous place, as residents do in a flood or fire alert.

clue.text: Force supporter to get over Tottenham Hotspur taking the lead twice

indicators.note: in a down clue, to get over means to sit above the next piece

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball

indicators.note: taking the lead twice means the opening letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A football fan has to get over Spurs going ahead twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporter' is not a fan but a golf tee. Tottenham Hotspur is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a law with bite has power or force to make itself obeyed.

clue.text: Sign of stone in Italy

parts.note: a precious stone is a gem
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A sign carved in stone somewhere in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Twins are one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Local man returns to English class able to solve problems with figures

definitions.text: able to solve problems with figures

indicators.note: returns means the dialect word for man is read backwards

parts.note: mun is a dialect form of man, as said locally in Wales and the north
a class or grade is a rate, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: A local fellow comes back to an English lesson and turns out to be good at sums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local man' means a dialect word for man, MUN (as in Welsh 'come on, mun'), which 'returns' reverses to NUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: someone competent with arithmetic and figures has basic mathematical skill.

clue.text: Objectively-speaking they died as gangsters

parts.note: the objective case of the pronoun they is them
ob, short for Latin obiit, means died, as on gravestones

explanation.surface: A grammatical aside reporting that some gangsters died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objectively-speaking' is grammar: the objective form of 'they' is THEM. OB (obiit) for died is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the Mob is the Mafia or organised crime in general, a body of gangsters.

clue.text: My author's terrible port

indicators.note: terrible says the letters are in a dreadful state and must be rearranged

parts.note: author's reads as author is, the 's working as a link

explanation.surface: A complaint that my writer is awful.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of author's stands for 'is', joining the fodder to 'terrible'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Great Yarmouth is a fishing harbour and seaside town on the Norfolk coast of England.

clue.text: Pepper old gangster every so often

parts.note: to pepper food is to season it
Al Capone, the Chicago gangster of the 1920s, gives AL

explanation.surface: Seasoning or shooting up some aged mobster from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pepper' looks like a noun or a hail of bullets but is the verb season.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: something tied to times of year recurs periodically, happening every so often rather than constantly.

clue.text: Point to or read up what Victorians put in puddings

parts.note: to point to something is to indicate it with an arrow; an arrow is a pointer

indicators.note: read up means the two words are read from the bottom of this down light to the top, backwards

explanation.surface: Instructions to point to something or research it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'read up' sounds like studying, but in a down clue it reverses TO OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a starch from a tropical plant used to thicken milk puddings in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: One that supports a parasite horde

definitions.meaning: an organism on which a parasite lives and feeds
a great multitude, as in a heavenly army

explanation.surface: A creature carrying a crowd of parasites.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the organism a parasite lives on, and a large crowd or army.

clue.text: Representative, following return of my son, cast out acid from vehicle? On the contrary

indicators.note: following means this part comes after
return of means the two pieces are read backwards
cast out means a piece is thrown out
On the contrary turns the instruction round: the vehicle is cast out of the acid, not the other way

parts.note: carbolic acid is phenol
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A long instruction about removing acid from a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' flips the deletion: the vehicle is cast out of the acid, not the acid out of the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something that stands for or represents something else is emblematic.

clue.text: Devious people, they're often pickled

definitions.meaning: slippery, evasive characters who wriggle out of things
snakelike fish sold jellied or pickled, a London East End dish

explanation.surface: Untrustworthy folk who are often drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pickled' suggests drunk, but these are fish preserved in jelly or vinegar.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: slippery fish preserved in jelly or vinegar, and people as wriggly and hard to pin down as those fish.

clue.text: European takes a risk about providing buildings

indicators.note: about means round the outside, so the word for taking a risk wraps around the word for providing

parts.note: to dice, as in dicing with death, is to take a risk
if means providing, as in provided that

explanation.surface: A European gambles on whether to supply something.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: grand constructions such as large buildings.

clue.text: Socialist rising against little beast is more astute

parts.note: a shrew is a tiny mammal

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means reading upwards, backwards

parts.note: a red is a socialist

explanation.surface: A left-winger climbing up against a small creature turns out cleverer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses RED in this down light; 'against' just means next to.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a comparative meaning sharper or shrewd in judgement.

clue.text: Cast off under manoeuvres, keeping low

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside
manoeuvres says the letters of the word before it are moved around

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

explanation.surface: A boat casting off while performing manoeuvres, staying low in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' looks like an adjective about the boat, but it is the cow's call; 'manoeuvres' shuffles the word before it to UNRED.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in sailing: a boat cast off has been released from its moorings.

clue.text: Rising swell American eating soft egg

indicators.note: eating means taking something inside

parts.note: US means American
p, piano, is soft in music
to egg on is to urge

explanation.surface: An American eats a soft-boiled egg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egg' is a verb, as in egg on, giving URGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a sudden increase, a surge or swell upward.

clue.text: Raised space in front of chief journalist

parts.note: an em is a printer's unit of space
a chief is a boss
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: Office talk: room cleared in front of the editor-in-chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a design that is raised stands out in relief from the surface.

clue.text: Gallantry award for 14 spelt out

definitions.note: 14-across is host, a presenter or master of ceremonies

indicators.note: spelt out means the letters are written as their names are said

parts.note: the MC, Military Cross, is a British gallantry award

explanation.surface: A medal for bravery, given for something written in full.
explanation.walkthrough: MC (Military Cross) also stands for master of ceremonies; writing the letters as said gives the American word.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a master of ceremonies is the host who introduces the acts.

clue.text: Talk of cake

definitions.meaning: to talk at length without saying much
a batter cake cooked in a grid-patterned iron

explanation.surface: Chatting about cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: verbose empty talk, and a crisp batter cake marked with a grid.

clue.text: Officer and men notice nothing in river

parts.note: Col is short for colonel, an army officer
OR stands for other ranks, the ordinary soldiers
an ad is a notice
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A commander and his troops spot nothing in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in river' is not a container: the definition is just 'river' and 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a major American waterway that carved the Grand Canyon.

clue.text: 'This plant is yellow,' child is told

parts.note: or is gold or yellow in heraldry

indicators.note: told means said out loud, so the word for child is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a kid is a child

explanation.surface: A child is informed that a particular plant is yellow.
explanation.walkthrough: Heraldic OR (yellow) is followed by a word for child as 'told', heard aloud: the plant's name said aloud sounds like 'or kid'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a flowering plant prized for its showy blooms.

clue.text: Former breakfast pastry is superfluous

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a croissant is French for a crescent, after its shape

explanation.surface: A croissant from the past is surplus to requirements.
explanation.walkthrough: The pastry is a croissant, whose name means 'crescent' in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an outgrowth that is unwanted or excessive is surplus to what is needed.

clue.text: Mark made in red not allowed

indicators.note: not says the word for allowed is to be absent from the colour

parts.note: scarlet is a bright red
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A red mark that is forbidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not allowed' reads as forbidden, but it says remove LET (allowed) from SCARLET (red).
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a lasting mark left on skin after a wound heals.
